items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Claude Dunson was playing in a big German band in one of these joints.

ctx.x: The manager of the Caveau had our permits to work in Belgium this time and we spent a lovely month there. Lily's trip to Germany had results for the band and I received an offer to play the month of September in Hamburg. That was rolling 'em Pete, because four months of steady work was very good for the band. We finished in Blankenberge the 30th of August, left the 31st and started working in Hamburg the first of September in a Dance Hall called Tanz Kasino Faun.

Herman Wilson had worked at the Faun with an American trumpet player named Claude Dunson and Herman spoke good German. The manager of the Faun could speak a little English and a little French also. Claude Dunson didn't speak German or French and I learned that whenever the manager of the Faun wanted Claude to change something, or he had something special he wanted to convey to Claude, he would say it in German to Herman, who would make the translation.

Herman sat on left end of the bandstand, and the manager started giving him messages to give to me. It would not have bothered me had I not known that the manager could speak and understand some English or French. I felt that my business with whoever was in charge of the place was between he and I, and not with my men. So I told this man not to tell Herman or any one else on the band to tell me what he wished from me, and if it concerned something special, I could always bring Lily to his office, and she would…
